 Injuries worry Farioli: Chris Smalling may not play again in 2026 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article The growing injury list is limiting FC Porto’s options. Chris Smalling is the latest absentee and the biggest concern, having suffered an injury to the medial collateral ligament in his right knee during the 1-0 win over Académico de Viseu that secured a place in the League Cup final four.
 According to Friday’s edition of O Jogo, Porto’s medical staff have opted for conservative treatment for the England international, hoping to avoid surgery that would keep him sidelined for several months.
 OneFootball Videos
 Even if his recovery goes well, the 36-year-old centre-back faces several weeks out. He is therefore not expected to return to action until after the end of 2026. That leaves Francesco Farioli with Jan Bednarek, Jakub Kiwior, Nehuén Pérez and Dominik Prpic as his options at centre-back.
 The coach also has other absences to contend with. William Gomes is recovering from a grade 2 sprain of his right ankle, sustained on 10 October in the 2-1 away win over Marítimo in the Primeira Liga. He is unlikely to be fit to play before the international break, scheduled for mid-November.
 Oskar Pietuszewski is also receiving treatment for a muscle injury in his left thigh, sustained in the 1-0 Champions League win over PSV. He is expected to miss the home league match against Estoril so he can return against Napoli on Wednesday, also at the Estádio do Dragão, in the European competition.
 There is still no return date for Vasco Sousa . The midfielder has not played since 14 December 2025, when he suffered a serious fracture of the fibula in his right leg while on loan at Moreirense. The injury occurred in the 4-0 defeat to Benfica at the Estádio Comendador Joaquim de Almeida Freitas.
 The four players are confirmed absentees for the match against Estoril in the tenth round of the Primeira Liga. The game takes place on Saturday at the Estádio do Dragão, kicking off at 20:30 mainland Portugal time, with Miguel Nogueira of the Lisbon Football Association refereeing.
 The matches Smalling, William Gomes and Pietuszewski are expected to miss
 Chris Smalling: Estoril (Primeira Liga), Napoli (Champions League), Vitória SC (Primeira Liga), Paredes (Portuguese Cup), Feyenoord (Champions League), Sporting (Primeira Liga), Santa Clara (Primeira Liga), Liverpool (Champions League), Estrela da Amadora (Primeira Liga), Famalicão (Primeira Liga) and Nacional (Primeira Liga).
 William Gomes: Estoril (Primeira Liga), Napoli (Champions League) and Vitória SC (Primeira Liga).
